main_text.l: REX CAR. MAVSOS[?]
ARTEMISIA R. HAL. VX. MA[?]
MAUSOLUS Cariæ regulus, quæ est in Asia minore,
obiit anno mundi 3586. ante Christum natum 376. huic Arte-
misia uxor fuit, quæ illum usqueadeo amauit, ut illius demortui
cineres vino mixtos biberit, alij dicunt aqua odoribus mixta:
præterea sepulchrum illi extruxit, quod ab Oriente cælauit Sco-
pas, à Septentrione Bryaxis, à meridie Timotheus, ab occasu
Leochares: priusquam id operis perageret, obiit Artemisia: nec
tamen recesserunt nisi absoluto iam, id gloriæ ipsorum, artisque
monumentum iudicantes. Plin.li.36.ca.5.
ARTEMISIA, Mausoli uxor, molita est, conseruandæ
mariti memoriæ causa, sepulchrum memoratissimū, dignatum
que numerari inter septem omniū terrarum spectacula. Id mo-
numentū Artemisia cum diis Manibus, sacris Mausoli dicaret,
agona, id est certamen laudibus eius dicundis fecit: proposuit
præmia pecuniæ, aliarumque rerum amplissima. Ad eas laudes
decertadas venisse dicuntur pleriq; diserti viri, inter quos Iso-
crates ac Theopompus, quem vicisse iudicatum est. Aul.Gel.
lib.10.ca.18.Boc.& Herodo.li.7.

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed on the engraved coins; the left one reads "REX CAR" and "MAVSOS" (the end of MAVSOLVS is cut at the edge, so the last letters are uncertain). The right legend "R. HAL. VX. MA" is hard to read and the abbreviations are uncertain. The ornament at the foot is a decorative fleuron with no text. "MAVSOLVS" is printed with V for both vowels and is given here as MAUSOLUS per the u/v rule. "Afia" is printed with a long s and is given as Asia.
